## What It Is

A side-project demo of an AI learning coach for junior engineers. You pick a
career journey, rate your skills, answer a few coach questions, and get a
pathway built from real course modules — then put the training on a calendar.

The learning content is aimed at Azure skills. The coach uses Google Vertex
Gemini when it is set up; if not, a local fallback still runs the demo. There
is no sign-in. Progress is saved in the browser. Use **Reset demo** if you
want to start over.

Live at
[pdp-assist.vercel.app](https://pdp-assist.vercel.app/){target="_blank"}.

## The Interesting Bit

You curate a library of training. The coach then builds a plan from that
library, tailored to the individual developer — their journey, skill gaps,
and how much time they can give. Same catalogue; different pathway for each
person.

## Next Steps

The demo is rough on purpose. Natural next steps:

- **From demo to workplace tool** — real sign-in and saved accounts, so a
  personal development plan survives more than one browser.
- **Capability frameworks** — map skills to something like the
  [DDaT Capability Framework](https://ddat-capability-framework.service.gov.uk/){target="_blank"}
  so pathways can support promotion evidence, not just a reading list.
- **A wider catalogue** — plug in Microsoft Learn, Pluralsight, or internal
  courses, while still only picking real catalogue IDs.
- **A closed loop** — finish sessions, reassess skills, refresh the pathway.
  Optional views for managers or L&D for check-ins and cohorts.
- **Calendar outside the tab** — export to ICS, sync with Outlook or Google,
  Slack reminders before a study block.
- **Nearby use cases** — graduate programmes, contractor onboarding, career
  switches (analyst to engineer), anonymised skill-gap views across a team.

Static learning catalogues are easy. Sticking to a plan is the hard part —
that is the gap this is aiming at.
